quotes.text: In Japanese, card testing is sometimes referred to as “credit master (クレジットマスター)” (abbreviated: クレマス).
If you use the latest Stripe Payment Element or Checkout, we have many automated and manual controls in place to mitigate card testing

To do so, you can use [custom rules](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/rules/reference.md#velocity-rules) in Radar, if [your plan](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/how-radar-works.md#compare-plans) supports this feature.

If you understand your customer behavior and want to customize the velocity of payments in detail, you can build [custom rules](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/rules/reference.md#velocity-rules) in Radar, if [your plan](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/how-radar-works.md#compare-plans) supports this feature.

old_evidence.text: To do so, you can use [custom rules](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/rules/reference.md#velocity-rules) in Radar for Fraud Teams. We cover that in the next section.

If you understand your customer behavior and want to customize the velocity of payments in detail, you can build [custom rules](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/rules/reference.md#velocity-rules) in Radar for Fraud Teams.

findings: The same canonical URL retains the card-testing definition, attack methods, detection symptoms, recommended integrations, risk-factor list, CAPTCHA, login, rate limits, key safety, retry caution, and combined mitigations. Most November changes are wording, punctuation, heading whitespace, and the new Japanese terminology note (new raw:9).

Two new passages condition Radar custom velocity rules on whether the merchant's plan supports the feature (new raw:123,137); the matched old guide explicitly named Radar for Fraud Teams (old raw:118,132). The current source at line 50 still states 'Radar velocity rules: custom rules for per-IP/per-account attempt limits (Fraud Teams)' without the new plan-availability condition.

A narrow source update should add the November raw to Raw Sources and adjust source line 50 to say custom velocity rules are available when the merchant's Radar plan supports them. The new guide does not identify which plans currently qualify; avoid treating this wording as proof that a different tier is eligible or that Fraud Teams lost eligibility.

The disputes concept at line 50 says only 'Radar velocity rules' without a plan entitlement claim. The stripe-radar concept's broader Fraud Teams descriptions draw on other sources and are not superseded by this single card-testing page.
substantive_changes: Radar custom rules for unusual behavior and payment velocity are now explicitly conditional on plan feature support (new raw:123,137 versus old raw:118,132). This affects how the source qualifies the control, not the list of suggested mitigations.
historical_claims_to_preserve: The old captured guide specifically recommended Radar for Fraud Teams for custom rules (old raw:118,132); retain the dated old raw reference rather than rewriting its historical wording.

The guide continues to recommend the latest Payment Element or Checkout for automated and manual card-testing controls, with effectiveness depending on integration data and risk factors (new raw:65,67; old raw:62,64).
conflicts: Current source line 50 presents Fraud Teams as the sole parenthetical availability qualifier; November guide lines 123 and 137 instead use plan feature support. This is an editorial qualification conflict, not evidence that a named Radar plan gained or lost entitlement.
unresolved_questions: Which exact current Radar plans support custom velocity rules is not established by this captured card-testing guide; the guide links to a separate plan comparison that was outside this job's matched-URL evidence.

answers.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/prevention/card-testing preserves the core card-testing guidance while changing the availability condition for custom Radar velocity rules. The old guide named Radar for Fraud Teams at old raw:118,132; the new guide says the account's plan must support the feature at new raw:123,137. The existing [[source-stripe-disputes-card-testing]] therefore needs a narrow qualification and new raw citation, while the Japanese term at new raw:9 is optional context.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/prevention/card-testing, retain the earlier Fraud Teams wording as dated historical evidence at old raw:118,132, and phrase current guidance as 'if your Radar plan supports custom rules' from new raw:123,137. [[source-stripe-disputes-card-testing]] line 50 presently lacks that condition. The recommended Payment Element or Checkout controls and their dependence on integration data remain supported at new raw:65,67 and old raw:62,64; this page alone does not establish the current eligible plan list.
